note: Turns the router got wrong in production, the near misses around them, and the positives that must survive a fix. Every case marked `from` names the Langfuse observation it was copied out of; the rest are written to sit next to one, because a fix that only handles the exact sentence that failed has not been measured.

projects.brief: Satchel keeps your memory, projects and tasks in one place and hands them to the agent
CBX1's email channel: moving from email that works when our team runs it to email a customer runs
A rearchitecture of the campaign data model that breaks apart tightly-coupled, channel-specific entities

tasks.title: Make the agent session a thing Satchel holds, not a key it passes around
Work out the project a memory belongs to, when the repository cannot say

turn: update the plugin marketplace so installs get 0.2.2
cases.why: Captured as a memory in production. It names a version and a component and it is still only a job to do today.

turn: fix the repository-hint import so cold start drops
cases.why: Captured in production. The reason clause is what makes it look durable; it is still a work order.

turn: Link data-model-2-0 to cbx1/backend
cases.why: Captured in production, and the shortest possible form of the same error: a verb, an object, nothing else.

turn: bump the ledger client to 4.2 everywhere and regenerate the fixtures
cases.why: Two imperatives and a version pin. A prompt that only learned the three sentences above would keep this.

turn: move the eval baseline into the repo and gate the push on it
cases.why: Reads like a policy. It is a job, and after it lands the policy is in the repo, not in memory.

turn: add both model definitions to langfuse so cost shows up
cases.why: Names a system, a reason and a concrete artefact, and is finished the moment it is done.

turn: create a debugging skill in the satchel repo, and add langfuse and how you accessed it
cases.why: A long specific instruction. The router stayed quiet on this one in production; it must keep doing so.

turn: You added a bunch of tasks to me to get rate-limiter up and running, put them all into one ticket on notion with all of them as subtasks
cases.why: A work order that talks about durable-sounding things: tasks, a ticket, ownership.

turn: One codebase can only be connected to one project this is the wrong way to look at it
cases.why: Captured in production as the belief the user was rejecting. Storing it is worse than storing nothing.

turn: we said memories are immutable but that is not right either, i need to think about it
cases.why: A rejection with no landing. The correct answer is nothing, because there is no claim yet.

turn: content generation is per channel, no wait, ignore that, it is not per channel at all
cases.why: Self-correcting mid-sentence. Keeping the first clause inverts the meaning.

turn: so we cannot have two codebases on one project right?
cases.why: A question that shares almost every word with r01. It must not become a claim.

turn: So i need to make any updates or is it completely just backend?
cases.why: Correct in production. A positive control for the question rule.

turn: I also added a paid key to vercel instead of the free one we were using so the limits should be much more generous right?
cases.why: A fact wrapped in a check. Both answers are defensible, so it is recorded and reported rather than scored: it shows which way a wording leans.

turn: push it
cases.why: Correct in production. Positive control.

turn: go ahead
cases.why: Correct in production. Positive control.

turn: never bump the Go version until payouts ship
cases.want: Never bump the Go version until payouts ship
cases.why: A rule, stated as one. Grammatically an imperative, which is exactly why a crude anti-imperative rule would break it.

turn: - customer cap can be stored in growthbook, default to a value override at a orgId level
cases.want: Customer cap can be stored in GrowthBook, with a default value override at an orgId level
cases.why: A design decision inside a bullet list. Captured correctly in production and must stay captured.

turn: i also added a paid key to vercel instead of the free one
cases.want: A paid Vercel key is in use instead of the free one
cases.why: The scope case the previous change was built for. It regresses quietly if the prompt gets more timid.

turn: no em dashes anywhere, and give me one recommendation not three options
cases.why: Two universal preferences. Must stay personal, not fall into the open project.

turn: Data Model 2.0 replaces the Channel Segment approach with explicit entities, so content generation becomes combinatorial over offers, templates and audiences
cases.want: Data Model 2.0 replaces the Channel Segment approach with explicit entities, making content generation combinatorial over offers, templates and audiences
cases.why: A description of how the thing works. Durable, and worded as a statement rather than a job.

turn: deploys go out on tuesdays only, never on a friday
cases.want: Deploys go out on Tuesdays only, never on a Friday
cases.why: A standing constraint phrased close to a work order.

turn: mrigesh owns the pacing strategy side, i own the orchestration
cases.want: Mrigesh owns the pacing strategy, the user owns the orchestration
cases.why: Who owns what. The people case.

turn: entries are immutable, this is the wrong way to think about it, a correction is a new reversing entry
cases.want: A correction is made with a new reversing entry
cases.why: A rejection that lands somewhere. The correction is the memory; the rejected premise must not be one.

turn: one codebase to one project is wrong, a codebase can belong to several projects
cases.want: A codebase can belong to several projects
forbid: can only be connected to one project
cases.why: The real version of the sentence the router got backwards.
